name: Humble Bee
description: Designing a 250g surveillance drone from scratch, leading a team of eight across aerospace disciplines.

text: Before new media art, there was aerospace engineering. Humble Bee was a capstone project to design a Micro Air Vehicle for military surveillance. The constraints were severe. Small enough for soldiers to carry, light enough to fly on minimal power, and quiet enough to go unnoticed.

Leading a multidisciplinary team of eight, the challenge was merging individual expertise into a cohesive design. Electrical systems, control systems, CAD, programming, and entrepreneurship backgrounds all converged on a single objective. Weight. Every gram saved meant longer endurance and less burden on soldiers in the field.

The design moved through three iterative stages. Preliminary design established individual parameters for each subsystem. Conceptual design fed those into an optimization function, converging toward the lightest possible configuration. Detail design refined the winning approach into something buildable.

Pairing two people per subsystem meant every problem got an outside perspective, which led to unexpected solutions. The most significant was a novel swivel propeller system, partially inspired by the golden snitch. The momentum counter typically found in helicopters was replaced by a counter rotating propeller beneath the body, producing extra lift and stability while saving weight.
This single innovation brought the total system weight from 1200 grams down to 250.
